exponential-growth.def: Growth by a constant percent each period, so the number added gets larger each time. It happens when resources are unlimited and gives a J-shaped curve (J-curve).

logistic-growth.def: Growth that is fast at first, slows as resources run short, and levels off at the carrying capacity. It gives an S-shaped curve (S-curve), with the fastest growth at about half the carrying capacity.

limiting-factor.def: A resource or condition that limits the growth of a population, such as food, water, space, nutrients, light, predators or disease.

density-dependent.def: A limiting factor whose effect grows stronger as a population becomes denser, such as food shortage, competition, disease or predation.

density-independent.def: A limiting factor that affects a population whatever its size or density, such as a flood, a frost, a fire or a drought.

population-density.def: The number of individuals of a population per unit of area or volume, such as 25 deer per square kilometer. Population density = number of individuals / area.
